title: Tensor dielectrics: eigenpolarization dispersion, birefringent slab transmission and tensor gradients

fixture.birefringent_slab: tests/test_tensor_slab_acceptance.py via benchmarks/tensor_cpml_birefringent_slab.py: exterior principal indices 1.2 and 1.4 with normal permittivity 2.25 filling the domain and both z CPML faces, slab principal indices 1.5 and 2.0 with normal permittivity 4.5, both rotated 25 degrees about z, thickness 0.6 um, wavelength 1.55 um, domain 0.5 x 0.5 x 6 um, transverse mesh 0.1 um, normal meshes 0.05 and 0.025 um (5x5x120 and 5x5x240 cells), CPML 1 um (20 and 40 layers), source z = -1.2 um, probe z = +1.2 um, Gaussian 6 fs FWHM offset 18 fs, 80 fs (594 and 1028 steps), float32 CUDA, TensorDielectricSimulation with cpml_material tensor and 8 checkpoints; per-channel normalisation to the slab-free run
fixture.bulk_eigenpolarization: tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py: PEC x walls, periodic y and z, 12^3 cells of 0.1 um, SPD tensor with eigenvalues (1.9, 2.6, 4.1) rotated 0.55 rad about x coupling Ey and Ez, modes (m = 2, polarization 0) and (m = 3, polarization 1), 400 steps float64; tests/test_anisotropy.py: Bloch box 6x5x5 cells with steps (0.1, 0.2, 0.25) um, fixed full SPD tensor, float64, one-step Fourier symbol, 256-step energy conservation, continuum refinement h = 0.4, 0.2, 0.1
fixture.tensor_gradients: tests/test_anisotropy.py six symmetric tensor components (float64, central difference step 2e-5); tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py rotation angle theta = 0.4 rad of spd((3.3, 1.5, 2.4)) through x CPML (float64, central difference 1e-4 and Taylor); tests/test_anisotropy_dispersive.py pole-strength rotation 0.6 rad; the slab index VJP d|t_1|^2/dn_1 at the coarse mesh against the transfer-matrix central difference
fixture.cpml_stability: tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py dense one-step spectral radius against the Becache-Fauqueux-Joly face criterion on a 5x11x5 Bloch box
fixture.pml: 1 um CPML filled with the exterior tensor in the slab study; 3 layers in the small tensor-CPML checks

precision: float32 CUDA for the slab study and the CPU-CUDA parity tests
float64 for the eigenpolarization, symbol, transpose and gradient checks
backend: cpu and cuda for the parity tests
reference_method: Per-eigenpolarization scalar transfer-matrix transmission t_j = exp(i k0 n0j d) / (cos(k0 nj d) + i/2 (nj/n0j + n0j/nj) sin(k0 nj d)) at normal incidence with shared principal axes (analytic continuum) and its central-difference derivative in n_1; closed-form discrete standing-wave frequency omega dt = 2 asin(S sqrt(lambda) sin(k/2)) with eigenpolarizations from eigh(inv(eps)[1:, 1:]) and its continuum limit; the independently derived Fourier symbol K_ab cos(q_a/2) cos(q_b/2) of the tensor operator; dense one-step matrices and full autograd of the same discretisation for transposes and gradients.

observables.name: channel_vector_relative_error
observables.definition: relative L2 of the two complex channel transmissions against the transfer matrix at 0.05 and 0.025 um

observables.name: channel_power_absolute_error
observables.definition: |t_j|^2 against the transfer-matrix power at the fine mesh

observables.name: index_vjp_relative_error
observables.definition: d|t_1|^2/dn_1 from the checkpointed adjoint at 0.05 um against the transfer-matrix central difference

observables.name: standing_wave_fields
observables.definition: E and staggered H after 400 steps against the closed-form discrete eigenpolarization standing wave

observables.name: continuum_frequency_ratio
observables.definition: |omega_discrete / omega_continuum - 1| for the coupled tensor standing wave

observables.name: symbol_and_refinement
observables.definition: operator against the Fourier symbol; discrete-to-continuum eigenfrequency errors at h = 0.4, 0.2, 0.1

observables.name: tensor_component_and_rotation_gradients
observables.definition: adjoint directional derivatives against central differences and Taylor remainders

slab.difference_from_common_criterion: the program asks 0.01 absolute on R and T and 3 percent on physical gradients; the slab study declares 0.03 on the transmitted channel power, measures transmission only (no reflection, no channel balance) and 15 percent on the coarse-mesh index VJP; docs record 0.0002 and 0.0014 power error and 6.89 percent VJP error

cuda_parity_float32.difference_from_common_criterion: gradient rtol 5e-4 exceeds the program's float32 rtol 1e-4

acceptance.source_of_limits: repository-recorded budgets; the program's slab_R_T_absolute_error 0.01 is not met by any tensor fixture because reflection is not measured

tests/test_tensor_slab_acceptance.py::te.oracle: oracle self-check: index-matched channels transmit one, weak contrast gives negative phase
scalar-channel transfer matrix transmission and its n_1 derivative, two meshes

tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py::test_pec.oracle: closed-form discrete eigenpolarization standing wave with a 3 percent continuum bound

tests/test_anisotropy.py::test_rotated_t.oracle: independently derived Fourier symbol; continuum refinement ratio below 0.27

tests/test_anisotropy.py::test_tensor_ad.oracle: central differences on six symmetric tensor directions

tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py::test_ten.oracle: central difference and Taylor remainder in the rotation angle; isotropic parity with the scalar path

tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py::test_cpm.oracle: Becache-Fauqueux-Joly continuum criterion against the dense discrete spectral radius

tests/test_anisotropy_cpml.py::test_rota.oracle: checkpointed adjoint against full autograd, float64

tests/test_anisotropy_dispersive.py::tes.oracle: central difference and Taylor remainder of the pole-strength rotation

tests/test_anisotropy_walls.py::test_cud.oracle: CUDA against CPU with walls and tensor CPML, float32

not_yet_covered: reflection and channel balance R + T of the birefringent slab (transmission only is measured)
oblique incidence, principal axes not shared between slab and exterior, and a 4x4 (Berreman) transfer-matrix oracle

tensor gradient against a continuum derivative other than the coarse-mesh n_1 VJP (15 percent budget); the rotation-angle gradient is checked against finite differences of the same discretisation only
asymptotic convergence order of the slab (two meshes only)

error_budget.precision_floor: float32 slab study: tail RMS to peak below 1e-3 bounds the finite-duration contamination, recorded 9.1e-8; float64 checks at 1e-9 to 1e-12
error_budget.time_window: 80 fs fixed across the two slab meshes (594 and 1028 steps); tail decay bounds the truncation; no window sweep
error_budget.pml: 1 um tensor-filled CPML fixed; docs/TENSOR_CPML_SLAB_ACCEPTANCE.md records no isolated CPML reflection measurement
error_budget.mesh: channel-vector error 1.372 percent at 0.05 um and 0.330 percent at 0.025 um (ratio 0.24)

notes: tests/test_tensor_slab_acceptance.py is added with this case as a thin wrapper of the benchmark whose CRITERIA were declared with docs/TENSOR_CPML_SLAB_ACCEPTANCE.md; the pilot at this commit reproduced 1.3721 and 0.3302 percent, channel powers 0.9880 and 0.8839 against 0.9882 and 0.8852, and an index VJP of -0.18468 against -0.17277 (6.89 percent), in 106 s on the shared RTX 3060.
